name: FortiADC Lab
tagline: Two datacenters, two FortiADC-VMs and a one-click demo cockpit for load balancing, SSL offloading, WAF and GSLB failover.
description: A fully virtual demo lab for **FortiADC**: server load balancing, health checks, persistence, SSL offloading, content routing, WAF and GSLB across two datacenters (Amsterdam and Frankfurt), **each with its own FortiADC**.

The two FortiADCs form the GSLB together: both are authoritative for the GSLB subdomain and auto-sync each other's virtual servers, so even losing a complete datacenter — FortiADC included — is absorbed, just like in production.

A controller container with a web UI rolls everything out: day-0 over the serial console, licensing, certificates from a private lab CA, SLB/WAF per datacenter and the shared GSLB config. Afterwards its **demo cockpit** lets you break servers, generate traffic and launch attacks with one click, and an Ubuntu desktop VM (RDP) is your window into the lab. Same approach as the FortiGate OT Lab.

requirements.label: Hypervisor
requirements.value: Proxmox VE host with root shell access

requirements.label: FortiADC-VM image
requirements.value: KVM zip: `boot.qcow2` + `data.qcow2` (one set for both FortiADCs), uploaded in the web UI

requirements.label: Licences
requirements.value: Two FortiADC-VM licences (VM02, 2 vCPU) — `.lic` file or FortiFlex token per FortiADC

requirements.label: Controller
requirements.value: LXC · 2 vCPU · 2 GB RAM · 20 GB disk

requirements.label: Whole lab (approx.)
requirements.value: ≈ 30 GB RAM: 2 × FortiADC (2 vCPU / 8 GB), desktop VM (4 vCPU / 6 GB), ~12 small LXCs

requirements.label: Network
requirements.value: Management LAN for the controller, FortiADC port1 and the desktop uplink; two management IPs for the FortiADCs

requirements.label: Internet
requirements.value: Needed once during deploy: Debian/Ubuntu packages, Ubuntu cloud image, Juice Shop and DVWA images

install.title: Interactive install
install.description: Choose **Default** or **Advanced** (storage, bridge, VLAN, DHCP/static IP, VMID range, dedicated host user). The installer prints the web UI URL and password when done.

install.title: Unattended install
install.description: Same choices as environment variables — see the header of `install.sh` for the full list (`NAME_PREFIX`, `CTID`, `LAB_VMID_BASE`, `HOST_ACCESS`, …).

install.title: Update an existing controller
install.description: Re-running the one-liner detects the controller and offers **Update**; the lab itself is left alone.

steps: Open the web UI on the URL the installer printed.
**Setup**: upload `boot.qcow2` and `data.qcow2`, set a management IP, gateway, DNS and admin password per FortiADC, and choose a licence per FortiADC (`.lic` or FortiFlex token).

**Lab → Deploy full lab**: bridges `vmbr800`/`810`/`820`, both FortiADC-VMs, the LXC template and all containers, the Juice Shop and DVWA images, the desktop VM, then day-0, licensing, certificates, SLB/WAF per datacenter and GSLB on both.
Wait for the desktop (about 15–30 minutes, status on the Lab tab), then connect with **RDP** using the address and credentials on the **Access** tab.
Run a demo from the **Demo cockpit** and follow the matching demo script (overview, load balancing, health checks, SSL, content routing, WAF, GSLB, visibility).

features.title: Load balancing & persistence
features.description: Virtual servers, pools, LB methods and insert-cookie persistence on a demo webshop.

features.title: Health checks
features.description: Flip a real server to an application error, a crash or slow responses from the cockpit and watch it leave the pool.

features.title: SSL offloading
features.description: Certificates from a private lab CA, TLS 1.2+ on the VIPs, HTTP → HTTPS redirect.

features.title: Content routing
features.description: One VIP routing on host and path to shop, portal and API backends.

features.title: WAF
features.description: Monitor vs. block, SQLi and XSS against OWASP Juice Shop and DVWA, exceptions.

features.title: GSLB with datacenter failover
features.description: Two authoritative FortiADCs with DNS delegation and auto-sync — take a whole datacenter, FortiADC included, offline.

notes: Day-0 configuration runs over the FortiADC serial console (`qm terminal`), so the FortiADCs need no pre-configuration — just the images and licences.
The controller reaches the host over **SSH** as a dedicated `adclab` user with sudo for only `qm`, `pct`, `pvesh` and placing two config ISOs. Revoke with `adclab-revoke`.
Lab bridges have no physical port; only FortiADC management and the desktop uplink sit on your network.
Add an application by adding a node, an `apps` line and a `virtual_servers` line to `lab/topology.yaml` — DNS, certificate, pool, health check, VS and GSLB follow automatically.
